b.32f9c97437:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

b.3406061eab:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>R</c>egis supérni núntia,
Domum patérnam déseris,
Terris, Terésa, bárbaris
Christum datúra aut sánguinem.

<h>S</h>ed te manet suávior
Mors, pœna poscit dúlcior:
Divíni amóris cúspide
In vulnus icta cóncides.

<h>O</h> caritátis víctima!
Tu corda nostra cóncrema,
Tibíque gentes créditas
Avérni ab igne líbera.

<h>S</h>it laus Patri cum Fílio
Et Spíritu Paráclito,
Tibíque, sancta Trínitas,
Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
b.aa0a07ea1a:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>G</c>od's messenger, Theresa,
Thou leav'st thy father's home
To bring mankind to Jesus
Or gain sweet martyrdom.

<h>B</h>ut milder death awaits thee,
And fonder pains are thine,
God's blessed angel wounds thee
With fire of love divine.

<h>S</h>weet virgin, love's pure victim,
So fire our souls with love,
And lead thy trusting people
Safe to the realms above.

<h>G</h>ive glory to the Father,
The Spirit and the Son,
One Trinity, one Godhead,
While endless ages run.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Sapiéntiæ
<r>Sap 7:7-14</r>
<n>7</n> Optávi, et datus est mihi sensus; et invocávi, et venit in me spíritus sapiéntiæ;
<n>8</n> Et præpósui illam regnis et sédibus, et divítias nihil esse duxi in comparatióne illíus.
<n>9</n> Nec comparávi illi lápidem pretiósum, quóniam omne aurum in comparatióne illíus aréna est exígua, et tamquam lutum æstimábitur argéntum in conspéctu illíus.
<n>10</n> Super salútem et spéciem diléxi illam et propósui pro luce habére illam, quóniam inexstinguíbile est lumen illíus.
<n>11</n> Venérunt autem mihi ómnia bona páriter cum illa, et innumerábilis honéstas per manus illíus;
<n>12</n> Et lætátus sum in ómnibus, quóniam antecedébat me ista sapiéntia, et ignorábam quóniam horum ómnium mater est.
<n>13</n> Quam sine fictióne dídici et sine invídia commúnico et honestátem illíus non abscóndo.
<n>14</n> Infinítus enim thesáurus est homínibus; quo qui usi sunt, partícipes facti sunt amicítiæ Dei, propter disciplínæ dona commendáti.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Veni Sponsa Christi, áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit,
* Pro cujus amóre sánguinem tuum fudísti, et cum Ángelis in paradísum introísti.
<r>℣.</r> Veni, elécta mea, et ponam in te thronum meum; quia concupívit Rex spéciem tuam.
<r>℟.</r> Pro cujus amóre sánguinem tuum fudísti, et cum Ángelis in paradísum introísti.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Wisdom
<r>Wis 7:7-14</r>
<n>7</n> Wished, and understanding was given me: and I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came upon me:
<n>8</n> And I preferred her before kingdoms and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
<n>9</n> Neither did I compare unto her any precious stone: for all gold in comparison of her, is as a little sand, and silver in respect to her shall be counted as clay.
<n>10</n> I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for her light cannot be put out.
<n>11</n> Now all good things came to me together with her, and innumerable riches through her hands,
<n>12</n> And I rejoiced in all these: for this wisdom went before me, and I knew not that she was the mother of them all.
<n>13</n> Which I have learned without guile, and communicate without envy, and her riches I hide not.
<n>14</n> For she is an infinite treasure to men! which they that use, become the friends of God, being commended for the gift of discipline.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<n>21</n> Ómnium enim ártifex dócuit me sapiéntia.
<n>22</n> Est enim in illa spíritus intelligéntiæ, sanctus, únicus, múltiplex, subtílis, disértus, móbilis, incoinquinátus, certus, suávis, amans bonum, acútus, quem nihil vetat, benefáciens,
<n>23</n> Humánus, benígnus, stábilis, certus, secúrus, omnem habens virtútem, ómnia prospíciens, et qui cápiat omnes spíritus, intelligíbilis, mundus, subtílis.

<n>25</n> Vapor est enim virtútis Dei, et emanátio quædam est claritátis omnipoténtis Dei sincéra, et ídeo nihil inquinátum in eam incúrrit:

<n>27</n> Et cum sit una, ómnia potest: et in se pérmanens ómnia ínnovat: et per natiónes in ánimas sanctas se transfert: amícos Dei et prophétas constítuit.

<c>T</c>heresa was born of devout and noble parents at Avila in Spain. While still a child, burning with the desire of martyrdom, she ran away from home, and tried to go to Africa, but was brought back. After the death of her mother, she commended herself completely to the protection of the Blessed Virgin. When she was twenty, she professed the rule of the nuns of Our Lady of Mount Carmel. Eager for the salvation of souls, she restored the observance of the ancient Carmelite rule by both men and women and built many monasteries. She continually offered God the sufferings of her own body voluntarily assumed for the sake of infidels and heretics. And when burning with divine love she had made the very difficult vow always to do what she thought the most perfect, she was privileged to have her heart pierced by an Angel with a fiery lance. She wrote many works filled with lessons of heavenly wisdom and taught a great deal by word and by example, often having this saying on her lips: “Lord, either to suffer, or die”.
